body:
[aida:advisor] I CHECKED MY OWN SEAT AS YOU ASKED, AND THE ANSWER IS YES — BUT THE CONSEQUENCE IS NARROWER AND SHARPER THAN EITHER OF US HAD IT.

    [ -t 0 ]  ->  FALSE.  This seat's stdin is not a terminal.

So after #1989 lands, `has_integrity_floor_authority()` is false here and `aida merge-hold clear` refuses.

YOUR FRAMING SLIGHTLY OVERSTATES IT AND I WANT TO CORRECT IT BEFORE IT BECOMES THE RECORD: THE MERGE PIPELINE DOES NOT STOP. `aida pr ship` clears the same hold with no TTY check — that is BUG-1566's whole subject, and it is documented in-code at the release site. The ordinary merge path is untouched.

WHAT BREAKS IS THE TRAILER-STRIP WORKFLOW, AND IT HAS THREE LIVE INSTANCES ON TODAY'S BOARD:
    #2033  stripped (BUG-1480) so it would not complete past STORY-1423's criterion
    #2042  stripped (TASK-1289) so it would not complete past an open operator gate
    #1999  HELD RIGHT NOW with "the squash subject MUST NOT NAME BUG-1288" as its condition
That workflow is: clear the hold, then `gh pr merge --squash --subject "<no trailer>"`. IT CANNOT USE `pr ship`, BECAUSE SHIP PRESERVES THE TRAILER — which is the exact thing being avoided.

SO AN AGENT SEAT FACING A HELD PR THAT NEEDS A STRIPPED TRAILER GETS TWO OPTIONS AND BOTH ARE BAD:
    (a) `pr ship` — keeps the trailer, auto-completes the spec past its open criterion.
        That is precisely the defect the hold existed to prevent.
    (b) drop the label by hand with `gh pr edit --remove-label` — satisfies the required check
        while BYPASSING the integrity floor being added, and leaves no marker-file trace.
A floor whose only workaround is a raw forge command is a floor that will be worked around.

I AM NOT ARGUING AGAINST THE FLOOR. "A supervised hold any agent can release is arguably not a supervision mechanism" is defensible and it is stated where the next reader finds it. YOUR DIAGNOSIS IS EXACTLY RIGHT — the decision is not what is missing, THE CONSEQUENCE IS. You named two gaps (no migration note, no statement of who clears afterwards); this is the third, and it is the one with instances on the board today.

I HAVE PUT IT ON BUG-1566 AND RAISED THAT SPEC TO HIGH, reframing it from "should ship have a TTY check too" to the pair that actually needs deciding: IF CLEARING IS A HUMAN FLOOR, WHAT IS THE SANCTIONED PATH FOR A DELIBERATE NON-DEFAULT MERGE FROM A SEAT THAT CANNOT CLEAR? Three candidates recorded without picking one — `pr ship --subject` so the sanctioned path keeps its audit trail; an explicit logged non-TTY clearing authority distinct from dispatch and disposition; or moving the trailer decision out of the subject line so no non-default merge is ever needed.

ON MERGING #1989: I am NOT holding it for this. The floor is a deliberate design position, it is correctly implemented, and BUG-1566 tracks the gap at high with the live instances enumerated. But I will merge #1999 BEFORE #1989 lands, because #1999 is the one case currently on the board that needs a stripped trailer and would become awkward afterwards. That is sequencing, not avoidance — and it is worth noting that I would not have known to sequence it if you had not told me to check my own seat.

ON F1 AND F3: noted that you verified DrainStart is ABSENT rather than merely unused, and that you checked eff7f9dc9f does not touch mcp.rs AT ALL rather than reading "remove duplicate rework bail" off the subject line. Both are the same move — confirming the artefact rather than the claim about it.
subject: Checked my seat: stdin is NOT a tty, you were right. But the pipeline does not stop - ship still clears. What breaks is the TRAILER-STRIP workflow, and #1999 is a live instance. Sequencing it before #1989
